sheet-1-1.description: The main part of sheet 6 of the Sanborn atlas of Park Ridge, November 1924, showing the centre of Montvale at 100 feet to an inch, with north a little to the right of straight up. It is bounded on the west and north by a heavy line separating it from the upper left part of the sheet. Grand Avenue crosses the part from west to east, and the double track of the N.J. & N.Y. Railroad (Erie Line) runs diagonally across it beside Railroad Avenue. North of Grand Avenue, Magnolia Avenue runs north past Wortendyke Avenue and West Drive, where block 32 is laid out in small lots with a few dwellings, a store and a lumber shed. South of Grand Avenue, Magnolia Avenue turns south west, and Franklin Avenue, Hamilton, Hopper Avenue, Wayne and Summit Avenue form a small grid of blocks 42 to 44 and 40, with frame dwellings, sheds and a post office near Magnolia Avenue. A park fills block 65 between Park and Magnolia Avenue. In the lower left the dash-dot borough line between the Borough of Midvale and the Borough of Park Ridge crosses the railroad; a toll house stands where it meets the road at the bottom. Much of the part is open ground with large numbered blocks (45, 46, 47) and scattered buildings.
notes: Magnolia Av. is today North Kinderkamack Road north of Grand Avenue and South Kinderkamack Road south of it (OpenStreetMap).
Grand Av. is today West Grand Avenue west of Kinderkamack Road and Grand Avenue East east of it.
Park is today Park Street, Hamilton is Hamilton Street, Wayne is Wayne Street.
Hopper Av. and Summit Av. were not matched to a modern street.
Magnolia Av. is drawn with a jog of about 75 ft at Grand Av.; the modern four-way junction there and Kinderkamack / Wortendyke were left out of the control.
The railroad is lettered N.J. & N.Y. R.R. (Erie Line); today the Pascack Valley Line.

Printed sheet 6 of the Park Ridge volume (November 1924), Montvale, 100 ft to an inch, two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 (main) around Grand Av., Railroad Av. and Magnolia Av. south of Grand (now South Kinderkamack Road), with Wortendyke Av. and West Drive; part 2 (upper left) Magnolia Av. (now North Kinderkamack Road) from Pearl St. down past Montvale Av., with Pearl Av., Pine, Walnut, Grove and River. North about 8 to 10 degrees clockwise of up.

sheet-1-2.description: The upper left part of sheet 6 of the Sanborn atlas of Park Ridge, November 1924, at 100 feet to an inch, separated from the main part by a heavy line. It shows the north end of Montvale along Magnolia Avenue, which runs down the left side of the part and curves at the top into Pearl Street, with Pearl River Road leaving to the north. Between Pearl Street and Montvale Avenue lies a dense paper subdivision: Pearl Avenue crosses Pine, Walnut, Grove and River, and blocks 8 to 15 are cut into many narrow numbered lots, most of them still empty. A few dwellings, an auto repair garage and an oil truck shed stand near Magnolia Avenue and Pearl Street. Pascack Creek crosses the lower part diagonally toward the heavy dividing line, near an ice house. West of Magnolia Avenue a narrow strip runs the full height of the sheet, past Brook and Cole Court, with scattered dwellings and stables set back on large lots. Key numbers of adjoining sheets (6, 7, 47, 48) are printed in the margins.
notes: Magnolia Av. and Pearl St. are today North Kinderkamack Road (OpenStreetMap), which curves from one into the other.
Pearl Av. is today Pearl Avenue; Pine, Walnut and Grove are Pine Street, Walnut Street and Grove Street.
Brook (now Brook Street) at Magnolia Av. was about 7.6 m off the fit and was left out of the control.
Cole Ct. is marked Arbitrary (name assigned by the map maker).

Printed sheet 6 of the Park Ridge volume (November 1924), Montvale, 100 ft to an inch, two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 (main) around Grand Av., Railroad Av. and Magnolia Av. south of Grand (now South Kinderkamack Road), with Wortendyke Av. and West Drive; part 2 (upper left) Magnolia Av. (now North Kinderkamack Road) from Pearl St. down past Montvale Av., with Pearl Av., Pine, Walnut, Grove and River. North about 8 to 10 degrees clockwise of up.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 7 of the Sanborn atlas of Park Ridge, November 1924, covering the eastern part of Montvale at 100 feet to an inch, with north slightly right of straight up. Montvale Avenue runs along the top, with a row of narrow numbered lots south of it, and Grand Avenue along the bottom. On the left, the double track of the N.J. & N.Y. Railroad (Erie Line) and Railroad Avenue cross the sheet diagonally, beside the lots fronting on Magnolia Avenue. The upper right is an almost empty paper subdivision of large blocks 16 to 22 on Short Avenue, Penn Avenue, Locust, Myrtle, Fairview Street, Main and Spruce. The lower half is a denser grid of narrow lots between West Drive, Waverly Place, Forest Avenue, Westmoreland Avenue and Hillcrest Avenue, crossed by Rutherford Place and Wortendyke Avenue, with Calle and Grand Place to the east. Building is light: scattered frame dwellings and garages, a few with stone first storeys. Midvale Public School No. 2 stands near Grand Avenue between West Drive and Waverly Place. Fairview Avenue leaves Grand Avenue to the south near the scale bar. Rutherford Place is drawn with a jog at Hillcrest Avenue. Large open areas on the right (block 25) and along the railroad are unsubdivided.
notes: Westmoreland Av. is today Westmorland Avenue (OpenStreetMap spelling); Locust and Myrtle are Locust Street and Myrtle Street, Main is Main Street.
Grand Av. is today Grand Avenue East; Magnolia Av. is North Kinderkamack Road.
Rutherford Place today continues east from Hillcrest Avenue at the north branch of the drawn jog.
Short Av., Fairview St., Spruce, Calle and Grand Pl. were not matched as control; Calle and Cole Ct. are marked Arbitrary.
The names along the top edge (Pine, Walnut, Grove, River) are cut by the sheet edge.
Midvale Public School No. 2: the school is named for Midvale, the borough name printed on sheet 6.

Printed sheet 7 of the Park Ridge volume (November 1924), Montvale, 100 ft to an inch, one part: Montvale Av. to Grand Av., Magnolia Av. (now Kinderkamack Road) and the N.J. & N.Y. R.R. on the left to Spruce on the right; a paper subdivision (Penn Av., Myrtle, Fairview St., Main, Spruce) in the upper right.
